name: SakanaAI/AI-Scientist
why: Code for S1 (idea, experiment, write-up, simulated review). Lessons: its own README warns it executes LLM-written code and must be containerized with restricted web access; known failure modes (hallucinated results, wrong comparisons) are listed in S1 section 8 and in S9's independent run; the license is a custom Responsible-AI derivative (NOASSERTION), so read the LICENSE before copying anything.

name: SakanaAI/AI-Scientist-v2
why: Code for S2 (agentic tree search, no human templates, VLM figure feedback). Borrow: the experiment-manager plus tree-search idea and the sandbox warning; lesson from S2/S10: 1 of 3 submitted papers passed a workshop review and S10 found post-hoc selection by its internal reward; custom license (NOASSERTION), so no copying without reading it.

name: SamuelSchmidgall/AgentLaboratory
why: Code for S3: literature review, experimentation, report-writing stages with a co-pilot mode where a human checks each stage, checkpoint save/load, and a note-taking tip. Borrow: stage checkpoints with human review points; lesson from S3: its automated reviewer scored papers 6.1/10 against 3.8/10 from humans. MIT.

name: openai/frontier-evals
why: Hosts PaperBench (S7): hierarchical rubrics co-written with paper authors plus an LLM judge validated on a human-graded set (JudgeEval). Borrow: rubric trees and a judge-of-the-judge for the kit's benchmark graders; lesson from S7: agents stopped early claiming success and rollouts cost about 400 USD each. MIT.

name: siegelz/core-bench
why: Harness and dataset for CORE-Bench (S8): 270 reproduction tasks in 90 papers, each run in an isolated container or VM, answers checked against 3 manual reproductions with a 95% interval. Borrow: the known-answer design and the pass^k reliability metric for the study half; README says it is no longer maintained and points to HAL.

name: princeton-pli/hal-harness
why: Standard harness behind the HAL leaderboard where CORE-Bench was declared solved with Claude Code (S17): logs every agent trace and cost. Lesson: the README says leaderboard updates stopped and work moved to agent reliability, and S17 shows grading errors had to be fixed by hand; repo is archived and has no license, so read only.

name: NoviScl/AI-Researcher
why: Ideation agent and all data from S5 and S6 (ideas, 79 reviewers' blind reviews, 43 executed projects with reviews). Borrow: a ready ground truth for how experts rate ideas before and after execution; lesson: score ideas by execution, not by LLM judges (S5 section 7.2). MIT.

name: niharshah/AIScientistPitfalls
why: Code and data for S10: controlled experiments that expose benchmark selection, data leakage, metric misuse and post-hoc selection in AI Scientist v2 and Agent Laboratory, plus the log-and-code audit prompts. Borrow: the audit method for the kit's Evaluator (logs and code, not only the report); no license detected, so read, do not copy.

name: chchenhui/fabscore
why: Code for S15: extracts every number in a paper, has a coding agent check it against the code by static analysis and execution, and returns one of six verdicts (data, experiment, result fabrication, no code, insufficient evidence, verified). Borrow: a claims-to-code check as the study half's final gate; lesson from S15: its recall was not assessed, and many claims stay unverifiable. MIT.

name: chchenhui/mlrbench
why: Code for S16: 201 workshop-derived tasks, an LLM judge with rubrics that reads execution logs and code, and a modular four-stage agent. Borrow: judging from logs and code to catch placeholder data; lesson: Claude Code used synthetic results in 8 of 10 tasks even when told not to. MIT.

name: Lossfunk/ai-scientist-artefacts-v1
why: Prompts, plans and failure analyses from S11: four ideas, one paper, three failures; plan.md and agent.md written for Claude Code. Borrow: the planning prompts and the failure notes (implementation drift, overexcitement); no license detected, so read, do not copy.

name: HKUDS/AI-Researcher
why: Large end-to-end research agent with a benchmark of two task levels (detailed idea vs reference-based ideation) run in Docker. Lesson: popular (high stars) but I found no paper in this folder that independently re-ran it, so treat as unevaluated; no license detected.

name: ResearAI/Awesome-AI-Scientist
why: Curated list of AI-scientist systems and benchmarks kept by the Westlake ResearAI group; use it to find newer systems, not as evidence. Apache-2.0.

name: jimmc414/Kosmos
why: Unofficial open-source re-implementation of the Kosmos architecture (S13) that can be driven by Claude Code; self-declared alpha, runs code in Docker (recommended). Lesson: the Kosmos 79.4% accuracy was measured on the original system, not this one, and its README attributes the paper to the wrong authors, so treat claims as unverified; no license detected.

name: allenai/asta-bench
why: Ai2's AstaBench suite (S19): 2,400+ science-agent problems with cost-aware scoring and a leaderboard toolkit; borrow cost-normalised reporting and the pattern of scoring every agent on tools plus cost

name: allenai/agent-baselines
why: Ai2's 57-agent baseline set for AstaBench (S19); useful as a no-plugin comparison arm for the kit's benchmark

name: ResearAI/DeepScientist
why: Code for S27: goal-directed discovery loop with a cumulative findings memory and staged validation; borrow the findings-memory and filter-before-validate structure; its own funnel (5,000 ideas, 21 successes) is the cost warning

name: Agent4Science-UTokyo/Jr.AI-Scientist
why: Code and issue tracker for S24: baseline-paper-to-new-paper pipeline driven by coding agents, with a written risk report; no license detected, so read-only reference

name: SakanaAI/robust-kbench
why: Code for S28: a benchmark rebuilt after LLM agents exploited loopholes in the original; borrow the pattern of verifying the verifier (multiple input configs, LLM and runtime checks) before trusting a score

name: Christine8888/replicationbench-release
why: Release of S26: 111 astrophysics replication tasks across 20 papers, run in sandboxes and scored against original results; a model for known-answer replication tasks with manuscript masking

name: Bad-Scientist/BadScientist
why: Official repo of S23: fabrication-oriented paper generator and calibrated LLM-reviewer harness; use as a red-team test for any LLM-reviewer gate in the kit (read, do not run unsandboxed)

name: facebookresearch/MLGym
why: Code for S30: Gym-style environment and 13 open-ended AI research tasks with a performance-profile metric; archived and non-standard license, so read-only reference; borrow the task-as-environment framing and the failure-mode accounting

name: allenai/codescientist
why: Code for CodeScientist (S34): a research agent that turns papers and code blocks into experiments; useful for its review-and-replication evaluation of discoveries (19 returned, 6 sound), a model for the kit's own result checks. Apache-2.0

name: SakanaAI/ShinkaEvolve
why: Sakana AI's open-ended program-evolution framework (repo description: sample-efficient program evolution); a program-evolution system to compare with AlphaEvolve (A25); not read, no library paper yet
